text: Okay, I think everyone is here. This is the release call for the new theme picker. Great. I can start with the beta if that works for everyone. Sure, go ahead. So the beta went out on Monday to about two hundred people. Switching themes now takes under a second, even on the old ThinkPad. The one thing still open is the preview on high-resolution screens. The thumbnails look blurry at scale two. I looked at that yesterday. We render them at the wrong size. I can fix it today. It's one line in a shell. Wait, is that the same bug we had with the wallpapers last month? Similar, but not the same code. The wallpaper one was a cache. How long do you think the fix takes, Ben? Half a day, maybe less. Then Anna can test it tomorrow morning. Tomorrow morning works for me. Can I add something about the installer? We changed the second screen, and the numbers look really good. Oh, nice. Tell us. Installs finish in forty seconds now, down from ninety. People stop at the disk encryption step much less now, but we explain why it matters. That is a big jump. It is. I want to do the same for the keyboard layout question next week. Let's do that. Ben, does that change anything on your side? No, it's only text and one picture. Carla can do that without me. One more thing, the plugin review for the weather widget is still pending. It has been four days now. Four days is long. Did we hear anything back? Nothing yet. I'll ping them this afternoon. If it's not merged by Thursday, we should ship the theme picker without it. Agreed. So to sum up, Ben fixes the blurry previews today. Anna tests them tomorrow. Carla starts on the keyboard question, and Ben chases the plugin review. Sounds good. Perfect. Thanks, everyone.
